title: Here Comes My Baby
feel: Riff on top-string triads, then strummed

sections.name: Verse / chorus cycle
sections.note: Verses cycle G–D–C–(G)–D; the chorus uses the same chords with a Dsus4–D decoration.

why: **Top-string triads as a riff**: C and D in first inversion (9-8-8, 11-10-10) and a root-position G (12-12-10), all on strings 3-2-1.
hard_change: **G triad (12-12-10) → D triad (11-10-10)**: the 3rd-string finger slides down a fret while the 1st string stays put.
theory: I–V–IV–V in G. G is a root-position triad; the D and C triads are 1st inversions (F♯ and E on the bottom).
steps: Changes alone, slowly: the three triads, one per bar.
With the rhythm at 70% (about 62 bpm), the riff then open strums.
With the record (form: intro, then verse and chorus three times, no bridge).
